open_points.subject: scratch limit scope over exchange I/O
open_points.text: “limits set by the runner before the code loads” and “one private exchange directory in which every file the code writes is bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`”
open_points.question: Does the per-file RLIMIT_FSIZE limit apply only to scratch files intentionally opened by agent code, or also to files the runner itself writes in the exchange directory while transporting inputs, outputs, trap reports or other protocol data?
options: It applies to every regular-file write by the runner process, including exchange-protocol files.
Runner protocol files are exempt; only files opened on behalf of agent code count.
The exchange protocol must avoid regular files after the limit is installed.
open_points.default_guess: Use pipes or precreated inputs for runner protocol data so the limit governs only agent-created scratch files and cannot impose an unstated cap on transport.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: A03 scratch-limit outcome detection
set_aside.text: “The size limit is the host kernel's own: the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” and “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”
set_aside.question: What observable fact makes a scratch-size limit count as “hit” and therefore `resource_exhausted`, especially when agent code catches the write error and returns conforming outputs?
options: The runner independently records every kernel refusal caused by RLIMIT_FSIZE, so the execution is `resource_exhausted` even if code catches it.
Only an uncaught write failure counts; caught failures may still end `succeeded`.
The outcome follows the eventual process result, making an uncaught exception `crashed` rather than `resource_exhausted`.
set_aside.default_guess: Have the runner independently record an RLIMIT_FSIZE refusal and return `resource_exhausted` regardless of whether agent code catches the error.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: A03 SIGXFSZ disposition
set_aside.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see”
set_aside.question: May agent code change the SIGXFSZ disposition after the runner ignores it, and if not, what mechanism prevents or detects that change so an oversized write cannot terminate the process and be classified differently?
options: Trap or forbid changing SIGXFSZ disposition.
Allow changes but still recognize SIGXFSZ termination as `resource_exhausted`.
Allow changes and classify resulting abnormal termination as `crashed`.
set_aside.default_guess: Trap changes to SIGXFSZ and preserve the runner's ignored disposition.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: scratch backing-store exhaustion
set_aside.text: “the directory as a whole has no separate bound in this release”
set_aside.question: If several individually permitted files exhaust the exchange directory's backing storage or inode capacity before any file reaches `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`, what outcome must `execute_function` return, including when code catches the resulting filesystem error?
options: Treat the exhaustion as `resource_exhausted`, independently of whether code catches it.
Expose the filesystem error to code; a caught error may still lead to `succeeded`, while an uncaught one is `crashed`.
Return `internal_error` or `stop_required` because host storage failed rather than a declared execution limit.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat an attributable ENOSPC or inode exhaustion during agent writes as `resource_exhausted`, even if caught.
